questions.question: The 11th Fundamental Duty provides opportunities for education for the ______ age group of children.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6-14 years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 11th Fundamental Duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
 
• It states that it is the duty of every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the **ages of 6 and 14 years**.
 
• This amendment also led to the insertion of Article 21A, making education a fundamental right for children in this age group.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of education in the development and empowerment of children, ensuring their right to free and compulsory education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution (Eighty-Sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, was enacted to provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years as a fundamental right.
 
• Article 51A (k) was added to the Constitution under Part IV-A (Fundamental Duties), which specifies this duty of parents and guardians.
 
• Education is a critical factor in the growth and development of an individual and the nation.
 
• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, commonly known as the RTE Act, was enacted to implement this constitutional provision.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: In which year were the Arms Act and Vernacular Press Act passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1878**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Arms Act** and the **Vernacular Press Act** were both enacted in the year **1878**.
 
• The **Arms Act** was designed to restrict the possession of arms by the Indian population, requiring them to obtain a license for the ownership of weapons.
 
• The **Vernacular Press Act** was implemented to curtail the freedom of the Indian-language press, allowing the colonial government to clamp down on publications that were critical of British policies.
 
• These acts were part of a series of measures taken by the British colonial authorities to tighten control over the Indian populace and suppress dissent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Vernacular Press Act** was specifically aimed at curbing the influence of the Indian press, which was becoming increasingly vocal in its criticism of British rule.
 
• The act allowed the government to confiscate the printing press, paper, and other materials of any publication that published content deemed seditious.
 
• The **Arms Act** was part of the colonial strategy to prevent the possibility of armed rebellion following the Revolt of 1857.
 
• These acts were widely criticized by Indian leaders and intellectuals as unjust and repressive measures that stifled the rights and freedoms of the Indian people.

questions.question: In which state of India is Kaziranga National Park located?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Kaziranga National Park** is located in the state of **Assam** in India.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, known for its significant population of the **Indian one-horned rhinoceros**.
 
• The park spans an area of approximately **430 square kilometers** and is characterized by its diverse flora and fauna.
 
• It is also home to large populations of **tigers, elephants, wild water buffalo, and swamp deer**.
 
• Kaziranga is recognized for its efforts in **conservation and protection of wildlife**, making it a prominent national park in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The state is bordered by Bhutan and Arunachal Pradesh to the north, Nagaland and Manipur to the east, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram, and Bangladesh to the south, and West Bengal to the west.
 
• Assam is also famous for its tea plantations, silk, and the Brahmaputra River, which flows through the state.
 
• The state capital of Assam is **Dispur**, located within the city of Guwahati.

questions.question: The Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rojgar Yojana (SJSRY) was launched in the year ________ by Government of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1997**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rojgar Yojana (SJSRY)** was launched in the year **1997**__ by the Government of India.
 
• SJSRY is aimed at providing gainful employment to the urban unemployed and underemployed poor by encouraging the setting up of self-employment ventures or provision of wage employment.
 
• The scheme focuses on providing skill development training to the urban poor to enhance their employability.
 
• It also includes support for the establishment of micro-enterprises by urban poor women and youth.
 
• The implementation of the scheme is done by urban local bodies (ULBs) with the support of state governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The scheme was restructured and subsumed into the National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM) in 2013.
 
• SJSRY had five major components: Urban Self-Employment Programme (USEP), Urban Wage Employment Programme (UWEP), Skill Training for Employment Promotion amongst Urban Poor (STEP-UP), Urban Women Self-help Programme (UWSP), and Urban Community Development Network (UCDN).
 
• The focus of the scheme was to provide sustainable livelihood opportunities through skill development and micro-enterprises, with a special emphasis on women and vulnerable sections of society.
 
• Under the scheme, urban local bodies were encouraged to form community structures such as self-help groups (SHGs) and community development societies (CDSs) to facilitate the implementation of the program.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common financial service provided by Micro Finance Institutions?

options.text: Investment advisory services for high-net-worth individuals
Small loans to low-income individuals for entrepreneurial activities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Small loans to low-income individuals for entrepreneurial activities**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Small loans to low-income individuals for entrepreneurial activities** are a common financial service provided by Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs).
 
• MFIs aim to offer financial services to those who are traditionally underserved by conventional banks, focusing on low-income individuals and small entrepreneurs.
 
• These institutions provide microloans, which can help individuals start or expand small businesses, thereby promoting economic development and self-sufficiency.
 
• Other services provided by MFIs may include savings accounts, insurance, and financial literacy training, but the primary focus remains on microcredit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Microfinance is particularly important in developing countries where access to traditional banking services is limited.
 
• MFIs play a crucial role in financial inclusion, helping to bridge the gap between the formal financial system and the underserved population.
 
• The microfinance sector has seen significant growth and innovation, with various models and approaches being implemented to reach more individuals.
 
• Regulatory frameworks for MFIs vary by country, but they generally aim to ensure the stability and sustainability of the sector while protecting clients.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for a governor for each state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 153**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 153** of the Constitution of India provides for a Governor for each state.
 
• The Governor acts as the nominal head of a state, while the real power is exercised by the Chief Minister and the state's council of ministers.
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India and holds office at the President's pleasure.
 
• The role of the Governor includes summoning the state legislature, giving assent to bills, and ensuring that the state's administration runs according to the provisions of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The role and powers of the Governor are also mentioned in other articles of the Constitution, such as Article 154 (Executive power of State) and Article 155 (Appointment of Governor).

questions.question: Which of the following methods is used to calculate national income by summing up the total spending on final goods and services in an economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Expenditure method**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Expenditure method** is used to calculate national income by summing up the total spending on final goods and services in an economy.
 
• It includes the expenditures made by households, businesses, government, and net exports (exports minus imports).
 
• This method is one of the primary approaches to measure the overall economic activity of a country.
 
• The formula for the Expenditure method is: **GDP = C + I + G + (X - M)**, where C is consumption, I is investment, G is government spending, and (X - M) is net exports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Value-added method** calculates national income by adding the value added at each stage of production.
 
• The **Output method** measures the total value of goods and services produced in an economy.
 
• The **Income method** sums up all the incomes earned by individuals and businesses, including wages, profits, rents, and interest.
 
• Each of these methods provides a different perspective on the economic activity and can be used to cross-verify the accuracy of the national income calculations.

questions.question: Ajmer Sharif is the shrine of which of the following Sufi saints?

• It is located on the border between **Peru and Bolivia** in the Andes Mountains.
 
• Lake Titicaca is also the largest lake in South America by volume of water and surface area.
 
• The lake has a rich cultural history and is considered a sacred place by the indigenous peoples living in the region.
